query: Which material can be used for enhanced catalytic activity and durability toward HER and HOR, and why?

generation.hypothesis: A compositionally engineered high‐entropy alloy (HEA) with a core–shell structure—where a core of refractory elements (e.g., Nb, Mo, Ta, W) provides durability and a shell is enriched with catalytically active transition metals—will exhibit enhanced catalytic activity and durability for HER and HOR compared to conventional monometallic or dilute alloy catalysts.
generation.material_initial_state: A conventional, homogeneous refractory HEA with equiatomic or near‐equiatomic composition.
generation.intervention: Utilize composition change through alloy design (via alloying or core–shell synthesis) to create a catalyst with a durable core and a surface layer enriched in catalytically active species.
generation.conditions: Electrochemical environments for hydrogen evolution and oxidation reactions, including both acidic and alkaline electrolytes under accelerated durability testing protocols.
generation.structural_mediator: Formation of a core–shell microstructure where the internal composition provides corrosion and mechanical stability while the shell tunes the surface electronic structure to optimize reaction kinetics.
generation.mechanism: The refractory core ensures structural integrity and resistance to degradation under harsh conditions, while the active shell modifies the surface electronic structure to lower the reaction overpotentials for HER and HOR. The synergistic interplay among multiple principal elements also helps in tuning the adsorption energies of hydrogen intermediates, leading to increased catalytic activity.
generation.predicted_outcome: The designed catalyst is expected to show lower overpotentials and higher turnover frequencies for both HER and HOR, along with improved long‐term durability under operational conditions, relative to traditional catalysts.
generation.baseline: Conventional monometallic or dilute alloy catalysts that typically suffer from either limited catalytic activity or durability under operational conditions.
generation.boundary: The performance improvements may depend strongly on the selected element ratios and the precise control of the core–shell structure; deviations in synthesis parameters could alter the balance between activity and durability.
generation.uncertainty: The optimal combination of elements and processing parameters (e.g., core–shell thickness, elemental ratios) needed to simultaneously maximize activity and durability remains to be fully determined.

falsification_experiment.design: Synthesize a series of catalysts including the proposed HEA core–shell structure, a homogeneous HEA (without core–shell distinction), and a conventional Pt-based catalyst. Test all samples under identical HER and HOR conditions in both acidic and alkaline electrolytes using accelerated durability protocols. Compare the overpotentials, Tafel slopes, and long-term stability through chronoamperometry and cyclic voltammetry.
measurements: Surface composition and structural imaging (e.g., TEM, XPS)
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the HEA core–shell catalyst does not display statistically significant improvements in lower overpotentials, favorable Tafel slopes, and enhanced long-term durability relative to both the homogeneous HEA and conventional Pt-based catalysts, then the hypothesis is falsified.

cited_evidence.text: High entropy alloys (HEAs), complex concentrated alloys (CCAs), and multi-principal element alloys (MPEAs) are the most common names of a new group of materials [ [1] , [2] , [3] , [4] , [5] ] introduced by Yeh et al. [ [6] ] and Cantor et al. [ [7] ] in the beginning of this century. Many definitions were proposed for such materials, but in general they consist of multiple (usually at least five) elements in equiatomic or near-equiatomic composition [ [2] ]. This approach is different from the traditional alloy design using one (or maximum two) principal element and other minor elements. The presence of many elements in equiatomic (or near) composition leads to high mixing entropy and thus to many interesting properties [ [2] , [5] ]. One of such effects is the existence of a random solid solution and simple body centered cubic (bcc) or faced centered cubic (fcc) structure. Recently HEAs with hexagonal closed packed (hcp) structure have been reported as well [ [8] , [9] ]. A new approach to HEA design using the valence electron concentration (VEC) was recently proposed with the aim of increasing the plasticity of these alloys [ [10] , [11] ].
